title: Teddy Weatherford and the Dreamland Cafe
summary: Wilson corrects himself to Weatherford and notes his style similar to Hines.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Somewhere were Teddy Wilson played some intermissions, or --

No. I don't remember Teddy working with the Grand Terrace. I remember Teddy Wilson worked the Vendome with Erskine Tate, and also had the band at the Dreamland, because that's where I worked with him, the Dreamland Cafe, 35th and State.
Must have been, oh, about 1925, somewhere around there.
Well, was Teddy here that early?
He was here that early, yeah.
No Teddy Weatherford I mean, not Teddy Wilson. Teddy Weatherford.
Yeah, Teddy Weatherford. Who was in that band?
You know, I can't remember who was in Teddy Weatherford's band.
He always sounded a bit -- the few recordings I heard of him, he sounded very much like Earl.
Yes, I know. He had that same style, that same swing style as Earl had.
Yeah, and the off-beats and the left hand --
The left hand, yeah. Very similar.
I wonder if they both arrived at that style by themselves, or --
I don't know how that happened.
